title: Finite internal normalization separates two nonlocal join centers
statement: Let $P$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, fix a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ [def-kun-separably-closed], and choose $P$-embeddings $H_i=P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ for two primes $\mathfrak q_i\subset P$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Let $J\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be the subring generated by the $H_i$, and let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(J)$. Suppose $J$ is a normal henselian local domain [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and both maps $H_i\to J$ are nonlocal, meaning that their inverse images of $\mathfrak m_J$ are proper subideals of $\mathfrak m_{H_i}$. There exist a finite separable field extension $K\subseteq K_0\subseteq L$ (finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space), its integral closure $P_0=\{x\in K_0:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }P\}$, and primes $\mathfrak q_{0,i}\subset P_0$ over $\mathfrak q_i$, such that $P_0$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K_0$, neither $\mathfrak q_{0,1}\subseteq\mathfrak q_{0,2}$ nor $\mathfrak q_{0,2}\subseteq\mathfrak q_{0,1}$, and there are compatible embeddings $P_{0,\mathfrak q_{0,i}}^h\hookrightarrow J\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending the embeddings of $H_i$. The two enlarged henselizations generate exactly $J$.

source.place: Agent-formulated internal-normalization refinement of the normalized-center comparison in the proof of Theorem 6.3, printed p. 13. The field K_0 is chosen inside Frac(J), not an arbitrary finite subextension of the ambient separable closure. The proof obligations concerning the centers and compatible enlarged henselizations are the content of this auxiliary node; they are not asserted to be elementary or to be the literal statement of Theorem 6.3. Online source read; local archival copy WANTED.
